recipes.name: Caramelized Chicken Wings
ingredients_raw: 12 large chicken wings, tips removed and wings cut in half at joint
1 teaspoon sesame seeds, or to taste

steps.text: In an electric skillet or a large skillet over medium heat, mix together the water, sugar, soy sauce, peanut butter, honey, wine vinegar, and garlic until smooth and the sugar has dissolved. Place the wings into the sauce, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes. Uncover and simmer until the wings are tender and the sauce has thickened, about 30 more minutes, spooning sauce over wings occasionally. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

raw_recipe.headline: Caramelized Chicken Wings
raw_recipe.description: Chicken wings simmer until tender in a sweet and savory sauce made with a touch of peanut butter.

review.reviewBody: The only reason I am only rating this at 4 stars and not 5 stars is because the sauce is SUPPER SWEET. I am going to play around with the amount of sugar & honey, but the overall flavor is great. I ended up using chicken breats (rather than wings). I cut each chicken breasts into 4 pieces and cooked the chicken in the sauce for about 15 minutes. Took the chicken out of the sauce (covered to keep warm) and then cranked up the heat, for about another 10-15 minutes, to thicken the sauce (be sure to stir more frequently as the sauce gets thinker).

Very good. I added red pepper flakes and a teaspoon of Thai red chili paste for a little heat to counter act the sweet. Thickened up the sauce a bit after the wings were cooked. Made a cornstarch and water slurry and stirred on medium high heat. Enjoyed them!

These were really yummy... I doubled the sauce because I made double the wings.... I followed the recipe and my sauce was pretty thick... after the 30 minutes uncovered.... I put my skillet under the broiler for 8-10 minutes checking on them every 2 minutes.... they were super sticky and delicious. Making again tonight the same way.

We loved this one! We didn't have wings, so I used thighs. I cut them into smaller pieces, nugget-sized. One of the other reviews commented on trouble with the sauce carmelizing, so I put the chicken and sauce in the oven for the second 30 minute instead of on the stove top. I used a cast iron skillet to cook the sauce and chicken, so it transferred to the oven nicely. The chicken was in the oven at 350 F for 15 minutes, and 400 F for the final fifteen. The sauce was wonderful, served with the chicken over a wild rice mix.

I used 15 wings instead of 12. I also took some of the advice from previous reviews and added a little bit of cornstarch and used 1/3 cup of sugar instead of 1/2. I seasoned the chicken with seasoning salt before hand but it made it slightly salty so if you’re not a fan of that, don’t do it. The sauce thickened for me but I admit I put it at a higher temp. When I let it simmer without the pot for the second 30 minutes it burned on the 15 minute mark, MAKE SURE TO FLIP THE CHICKEN IT WILL BURN. Also, this recipe doesn’t tell you that the peanut butter is impossible to stir in so it’s gonna look weird at first but it will turn out great. Overall, great tasty recipe, family said they liked it, will make it again. Very simple.

Really nice recipe. As others had said it was very sweet I cut the sugar to about 1/4 cup brown sugar instead of white. I also left out the peanut butter. The sauce is like a honey sesame sauce. I used a pressure cooker to cook the wings for 30 minutes and then reduced the sauce in about 15 minutes. Tender and delicious. Will definitely be making it again.

I thought these wings were incredibly good. I did them for the super bowl and again tonight because we enjoyed them so much. I changed a few things out of necessity, I used balsamic vinegar and natural peanut butter as that is what I had on hand. I also found both times that I prepared them that the thirty minutes uncovered part of the recipe was inadequate to get the stickiness I wanted. The sauce was still a bit soupy at that point. I left them uncovered on medium heat for an extra twenty minutes and that did the trick. That being said the culprit could easily have been my aging electric range. Either way we love this recipe.

My family and I love this recipe. I normally make the recipe exactly as written but last night I substituted the chicken wings for hand-breaded, pan fried chicken breasts chunks that I pre-cooked and I added about 2t of crushed red pepper. I then tossed the chicken in the wings sauce along with steamed broccoli. I serviced over white rice and garnished with sesame seeds (I submitted a photo). If you ask my husband he’d say it was Generals Chicken. If you asked my son (13yo) he’d say it was boneless wings. If you ask me, I call it a success as they both had seconds.
I've made this recipe a ton of times. It's a hit with my friends. The only thing I do differently is I fry the wings naked. Then, I simmer them in the sauce.

Both family and friends did love this. No sesame seeds allergy. I've already made it three time and this last was simply perfect. I used 2 lbs of chopped tigs (cut in half). Starting from the 6 servings I made few adjustments according to my taste and previous 'tests':
- Used 1/3 packed dark brown sugar and 3 TBs of White sugar (to better thicken the sauce at the end of cooking but keeping acceptable the sweetness)
- 3 TBs of honey (not only 1)
- Added 3 TBs of ketchup
- Used cider vinegar instead of wine vinegar.
Smothed into the pot with a blender then cooked followings directions... no need to use cornstarch. 
The result was just perfect and 'mamma mia' ;) ... lucky i took the pic before placing it on the table!

Made this recipe exactly and the wings turned out gooey and melt in your mouth tasty, although in no way resembled the photo. The charring in the photo suggests some grilling or broiling, which is absent from the recipe directions.

Our Millennial suggested cooking the sauce according to directions and either deep frying or baking the wings separately, then applying the sauce afterwards. This would result in the wings having some characteristic chicken wing "chew" to them, which is otherwise completely absent from effectively being boiled in the sauce for an hour.

As for sauce thickening, it happens rather quickly during the last 5 minutes of cooking - no need to add corn starch. If you wish to speed up thickening, just raise the temperature, but be sure to keep an eye on the wings or the sauce will quickly turn to tar.

Four stars because of no chicken wing "chew".
This is a great recipe but like others wrote, to sweet, so I eliminate the sugar and double the honey and 2 x peanut butter and I add ginger too.
These wings are delicious -- a great alternative for those who don't like hot spicy wings. They are a sweet flavor that you just can't stop eating! Yummy!!

These wings are a sweet alternative to hot wings. Unfortunately, the sweetness is a little one-note -- tasting sweet with a faint taste of peanut butter on occasion. I think the sauce may need more soy and peanut butter to round out the flavor. I used a white wine vinegar since it did not specify. To those who could not get the sauce to thicken, simply turn the heat up so that the sauce boils (aka, make a reduction). It will take maybe 10 minutes to boil off the excess water, but it will happen and you don't need to add any thickeners. Watch it carefully as once the water is gone it could burn easily.
Worked for me, the sauce did thicken, i put a bit less sugar even and didn't even need all 30min, sauce was thick and it had reduced

Thank you for a TREMENDOUS recipe! The hubs and I LOVED IT! I did make 2 changes - since we try to keep our simple carbs on the low side, I used Lakanto sweetner instead of sugar, and I also used a few shakes of Sesame Oil when I test-tasted the wonderful sauce, as it had a decided Thai flavor. I saved the leftover sauce for another day. SO GOOD!
DELICIOUS! So easy to make!
I've made this recipe repeatedly as Shannon wrote it, for years, and it is delicious!!!
The wings were wonderful. So tender and delicious.

This was absolutely delicious and my family loved it. The only thing I did differently was to sprinkle the wings with onion powder and garlic powder before cooking. Will be making this my go to wings recipe. Thank you!
